content.title: Kentucky Derby 2026: Commandment and Further Ado Lead Points Standings
content.text: Published Apr 12, 2026 - 03:40 25 Reads Last Update Apr 12, 2026 - 03:40 Smallest Font Largest Font Commandment and Further Ado, both trained by Louisville native Brad Cox, currently lead the 2026 Kentucky Derby points leaderboard, as reported on Friday, April 11, 2026. Renegade, trained by Todd Pletcher, secures the third position in the standings for the prestigious Run for the Roses at Churchill Downs.EquestrianThe Kentucky Derby, scheduled for May 2 at Churchill Downs, will feature the top 20 horses from the final points standings. Additionally, two horses from the Euro/Mideast Road to the Kentucky Derby and one from the Japan Road to the Kentucky Derby will receive invitations. In the event of a tie in the points standings, earnings from non-restricted stakes races will be used as the tie-breaker. Several top contenders have already arrived at Churchill Downs to train for the 152nd running of the event. Further Ado, who recently reclaimed the top spot in Byron King’s Derby Dozen after an 11-length victory in the April 4 Toyota Blue Grass Stakes, has won two out of two races at Keeneland with an average winning margin of 15.5 lengths. He previously secured a victory at Churchill Downs in the Kentucky Jockey Club Stakes last fall.Horse & Dog Racing Renegade, this year’s Arkansas Derby and Sam F. Davis Stakes winner, closed as the 4-1 favorite in the final Kentucky Derby Future Wager offered by Churchill Downs. This indicates significant backing from bettors for the colt, who also leads the National Thoroughbred Racing Association’s Top 3-Year-Old Poll.Commandment earned a 101 Beyer Speed Figure in the Curlin Florida Derby on March 28, the second-highest among three-year-olds behind Further Ado's 106 Blue Grass Beyer Speed Figure. His determined head victory over The Puma marked him as a resolute and capable colt. Trainer Chad Brown confirmed that Emerging Market, winner of the Grade 2 Louisiana Derby, is definitively headed to the Kentucky Derby. However, Brown is still deciding on the participation of Blue Grass (G1) runner-up Ottinho and seventh-place Wood Memorial (G2) finisher Iron Honor, both of whom have invitations.“I’m hoping to make a decision once we get past this weekend,” Brown stated on Friday in a phone call to reporters. “I’m still talking to the respective owners and observing the horses and observing the prospective field for the Derby.”Brown typically waits at least two weeks after a race before breezing his horses again. Ottinho and Iron Honor competed last Saturday, and Derby entries are due in two weeks on April 25. This timeline presents a challenge between patience and urgency for the five-time Eclipse Award-winning trainer. Potente, another prominent contender, incurred his first defeat when finishing second in the Santa Anita Derby. Trainer Bob Baffert, seeking a record seventh Kentucky Derby win, will rely on Potente as his sole Derby starter.Trainer Mark Casse aims for his first Kentucky Derby victory after 11 previous starters, none of whom have achieved a top-three finish. Silent Tactic, one of his entrants, has finished first or second in all six of his starts, with his strongest performance being a win in the Southwest Stakes.EquestrianMichael McCarthy-trained Stark Contrast, a turf specialist who finished second in the Jeff Ruby Steaks (G3), is unlikely to run in the Kentucky Derby. McCarthy indicated that the American Turf (G1) would be a more suitable race for the undefeated turf runner, according to his comments on “At the Races” on Monday. The 152nd Kentucky Derby will be broadcast on NBC, Peacock, USA Network, and other NBCU platforms. Post time for the race is set for 6:57 p.m. on Saturday, May 2. 0 Like 0 Dislike 0 Funny 0 Angry 0 Sad 0 Wow
